paras.text: Abstract. Visibility forecasting at airports is a hard problem because low-visibility events are rare, strongly stratified, and driven by interactions between radiative cooling, turbulence and advection that numerical models resolve only partially. Statistical post-processing offers a practical alternative. Instead of resolving the microphysics, it learns a mapping from predictors that are already available from the numerical model to the probability of the target event, using a long archive of historical observations as the training signal.
paras.text_raw:
Abstract. Visibility forecasting at airports is a hard problem because low-visibility events are rare, strongly stratified, and driven by
interactions between radiative cooling, turbulence and advection that numerical models resolve only partially. Statistical
post-processing offers a practical alternative. Instead of resolving the microphysics, it learns a mapping from predictors that are
already available from the numerical model to the probability of the target event, using a long archive of historical observations as
the training signal.

Instead of resolving the microphysics, it learns a mapping from predictors that are already available from the numerical model to the probability of the target event, using a long archive of historical observations as the training signal.

body_paragraphs.text: Statistical post-processing offers a practical alternative. Instead of resolving the microphysics, it learns a mapping from predictors that are already available from the numerical model to the probability of the target event, using a long archive of historical observations as the training signal.

body_paragraphs.text: The predictor set matters more than the learning algorithm in most published comparisons. Ceiling, runway visual range, dew point depression and boundary layer height carry most of the signal, while radiation terms add skill only during the evening transition when the boundary layer collapses rapidly.
